title: Bonsai 27B: A 1-Bit Model Small Enough for Your Browser (and Maybe Your Phone)
hook: 1-bit quantization shrinks a 27B dense model from 54GB to 3.8GB — a 93% cut — while keeping about 90% of its original capability, per the release.
key_points: PrismML released Bonsai 27B, a 27B-parameter dense LLM (built on Qwen3.6-27B) quantized down to 1 bit per weight.
Shrinks it from 54GB to 3.8GB (a 93% cut); across 15 benchmarks it averages 76.1 vs 85.1 for the full-precision original (~90% retained).
True 'binary g128' quantization: one sign bit per weight, groups of 128 share an FP16 scale (~1.125 bits/weight) — no higher-precision layers.
Even the embeddings, attention/MLP projections, and LM head are binary — most 1-bit schemes keep some layers at higher precision.
Small enough to run entirely client-side in a web browser via custom WebGPU kernels, no server round-trip needed.
The community has framed the same release as the first 27B-parameter-class model able to run on a phone.
content_html: The PrismML team released Bonsai 27B, a dense 27-billion-parameter LLM quantized all the way down to 1 bit per weight. That extreme compression takes the model from 54GB to just 3.8GB — a 93% reduction — while the release claims it retains roughly 90% of the original model's "intelligence." The model is small enough to run entirely client-side in a browser via custom WebGPU kernels, with no server needed.
extra_html: Community reaction (via a companion r/LocalLLaMA post) framed the same release differently: as the first 27B-parameter-class model that can run on a phone, since a 3.8GB footprint fits where a 54GB one never could. A follow-up post filled in the technical detail behind the compression: it's true "binary g128" quantization — every weight collapses to a single sign bit, with each group of 128 weights sharing one FP16 scale, landing at roughly 1.125 bits per weight and no higher-precision escape hatches. Unusually, that includes the embeddings, attention/MLP projections, and even the LM head — most 1-bit schemes keep at least some of those layers at higher precision. Across 15 benchmarks, Bonsai 27B (built on Qwen3.6-27B) averages 76.1 versus 85.1 for the full-precision original. PrismML published it as a Hugging Face collection, alongside a live WebGPU demo space for trying it directly in-browser — no install required.

related.title: Unsloth's NVFP4 Qwen3.6 Quants Beat NVIDIA's Own — by Actually Using 4-bit Math
related.hook: Unsloth's NVFP4 quants for Qwen3.6 run up to 2.5x faster than NVIDIA's official NVFP4 release, with no measured accuracy loss — by quantizing activations too, not just weights.
